items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I called Mr. Tripet who was the owner of the Chikito and told him what happened.

ctx.x: We started in the Chikito on Tuesday the 16th, had the Christmas night off. We were paid every Monday night, and our first pay came on the 22nd. It was the 29th when we received our second week's salary, minus the Christmas night that we didn't work. Zutty had asked me to be paid in dollars and that's how I paid him. So this time, when I gave him his salary and he counted it, he told me that it was not the right amount. I told him it was right because we were not paid for the night we didn't work. He was salty as…

The next afternoon, I heard from someone that Zutty had left. I called Mr. Tripet who was the owner of the Chikito and told him what happened. Ofcourse, Zutty couldn't be stopped from leaving the country, but Tripet could have had his baggages held the same as the French agent named Canetti had done to Louis Armstrong in the 1930's when Pops left for New York before playing an engagement, Canetti had booked for him. But Zutty had gotten away too early. However, as he and I were members of the 802 musicians union…

Later, I read an interview that Zutty gave to a jazz magazine that he had been working with me in Europe for peanuts which was to say that I paid him a small salary. He had 250 dollars a week with me which was a good salary anywhere in 1952 and there are musicians in the U.S.A. today that don't make a salary like that for a week's work. And he didn't mention that on the tour he did in Europe with Mezz Mezrow, he only had 200 dollars a week. And that's a fact that I know is true.
